$comment: WHAT THIS FILE DESCRIBES, RECORDED 2026-10-08 after a contract audit claimed a status/verdict drift against the artifact emitter. This schema is bound to the PROFILE documents design-lab/production/profiles/preflight-{print,digital,video}.json: they carry const schemaVersion design-lab/preflight/v2 and exactly the four top-level fields required here (preflight_id, schemaVersion, profile, required_checks), and design-lab/scripts/verify_production_preflight.py validates them against this file. The optional nested `result` (status: pass|fail, checks[].status) is the second half named in the description -- the machine-readable report read by src/design_lab/assurance/handoff_readiness.py::_preflight_gates, which expects preflight['result']['status'] alongside preflight['required_checks']. Nothing in this file requires a TOP-LEVEL `status`: `status` is not in `required` and appears only under `result.properties`. The artifact report emitted by src/design_lab/assurance/production_preflight.py is a different contract with its own version (design-lab/artifact-preflight/v1), a top-level `verdict`, and no `result` object; it is schema-bound to schemas/artifact-preflight.schema.json, NOT here. Do not 'align' the emitter to this file: that would rename a field apps/workbench reads from the HTTP response today, and would force profile-only fields (preflight_id, required_checks) into a report that has no business declaring them.
